package_info.why_malicious: The Shinra ransomware encrypts user files, deletes system recovery data, manipulates system settings to inhibit recovery, exfiltrates data, and demands ransom for decryption. It also attempts to evade detection and recovery by terminating processes/services, clearing logs, and modifying registry keys.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Copy itself to the current user's startup folder as <ID>.exe, where <ID> is 32 hex characters.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the malware copies itself to the user's startup folder with a randomized name, ensuring persistence across reboots.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Self-replication to the startup folder is a common persistence technique used by malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not silently copy itself to startup without user consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate installers may add startup entries, but not with randomized names or without user notification.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Terminate processes whose names contain: supervise, Defwatch, winword, QBW32, QBDBMgr, qbupdate, axlbridge, httpd, fdlauncher, MsDtSrvr, java, 360se, 360doctor, wdswfsafe, fdhost, GDscan, ZhuDongFangYu, QBDBMgrN, mysqld, AutodeskDesktopApp, acwebbrowser, Creative Cloud, Adobe Desktop Service, CoreSync, Adobe CEF, Helper, node, AdobeIPCBroker, sync-taskbar, sync-worker, InputPersonalization, AdobeCollabSync, BrCtrlCntr, BrCcUxSys, SimplyConnectionManager, Simply.SystemTrayIcon, fbguard, fbserver, ONENOTEM, wsa_service, koaly-exp-engine-se
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the malware enumerates running processes and terminates those matching a hardcoded list, targeting security, productivity, and database applications to maximize file encryption impact.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Terminating a wide range of processes, especially security and productivity tools, is a hallmark of ransomware aiming to maximize damage.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal applications do not indiscriminately kill unrelated processes.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Rarely, uninstallers may terminate their own processes, but not such a broad set.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Terminate services whose names contain: SavRoam, Sqlservr, sqlagent, sqladhlp, Culserver, RTVscan, sqlbrowser, SQLADHLP, QBIDPService, Intuit.QuickBooks.FCS, QBCFMonitorService, msmdsrv, tomcat6, zhudongfangyu, vmware-usbarbitator64, vmware-converter, dbsrv12, dbeng8, MSSQL$MICROSOFT##WID, MSSQL$VEEAMSQL2012, SQLAgent$VEEAMSQL2012, SQLBrowser, SQLWriter, FishbowlMySQL, MSSQL$MICROSOFT##WID, MySQL57, MSSQL$KAV_CS_ADMIN_KIT, MSSQLServerADHelper100, SQLAgent$KAV_CS_ADMIN_KIT, msftesql-Exchange, MSSQL$MICROSOFT##SSEE, MSSQL$SBSMONITORING, MS
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the malware enumerates and terminates services matching a hardcoded list, focusing on database, backup, and security services to ensure files are not locked and can be encrypted.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Disabling critical services is a common ransomware tactic to ensure maximum file encryption and to disable recovery.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not terminate unrelated or critical system services.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Set registry key HKCU\Control Panel\Desktop\Wallpaper to C:\ProgramData\<ID>.bmp
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the malware changes the desktop wallpaper by modifying the registry to display a ransom note or warning image.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Changing the desktop wallpaper to a ransom note is a classic ransomware tactic.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate applications do not change user wallpaper without consent.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Set registry keys: HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\OEMInformation\Manifucator, SupportPhone; HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System\legalnoticecaption = 'Encrypted by Kuza', legalnoticetext = 'Email us for recovery: ethan@...'
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the malware sets registry keys to display a legal notice with ransom instructions on system startup.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Setting legal notice text to ransom instructions is a direct indicator of ransomware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not set legal notices to extort users.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Use wevtutil.exe to enumerate and clear Windows logs.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the malware executes wevtutil.exe to enumerate and clear Windows event logs, erasing evidence of its activity.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Clearing event logs is an anti-forensics technique to hinder incident response.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not clear system logs without explicit user/admin action.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Use COM to run: SELECT * FROM Win32_ShadowCopy; C:\Windows\System32\wbem\WMIC.exe shadowcopy where "ID='%s'" delete
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the malware enumerates and deletes all Volume Shadow Copies using WMI and WMIC, preventing file recovery.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Deleting shadow copies is a well-known ransomware tactic to prevent recovery.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not delete all shadow copies without user consent.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the malware encrypts files and appends a unique extension to mark them as encrypted.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Appending unique extensions to encrypted files is a ransomware signature.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not encrypt user files and rename them with ransom-related extensions.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Execute: bcdedit.exe /set {default} bootstatuspolicy ignoreallfailures; bcdedit.exe /set {default} recoveryenabled no
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the malware disables Windows recovery and repair functions by modifying boot configuration, making system recovery more difficult.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Disabling recovery options is a tactic to increase ransom pressure.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not disable system recovery without user/admin approval.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Restart itself using 'runas admin' to ensure administrator privileges.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the malware attempts to elevate its privileges by restarting itself as administrator.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Privilege escalation is a common malware tactic to bypass security restrictions.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software requests elevation transparently and for valid reasons.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Silently empty the Recycle Bin without user confirmation, progress bar, or sound.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the malware empties the Recycle Bin to remove traces of deleted files.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Silently emptying the Recycle Bin is an anti-forensics measure.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not empty the Recycle Bin without user action.

attack_chain.action: Malware is executed and copies itself to the startup folder for persistence.
Malware terminates processes and services to maximize file access and disable security/backup.
Malware disables recovery mechanisms by deleting shadow copies and modifying boot configuration.

attack_chain.leads_to: Ensures all malicious actions can be performed.

attack_chain.action: Malware encrypts files and appends custom extensions.
attack_chain.leads_to: Files are rendered inaccessible to the user.

attack_chain.action: Malware drops ransom note and changes desktop wallpaper/legal notice.
attack_chain.leads_to: User is notified of ransom demand.

attack_chain.action: Malware clears event logs and empties Recycle Bin to cover tracks.

behavioral_signatures: Mass process/service termination targeting security, backup, and productivity software
Deletion of Volume Shadow Copies via WMI/WMIC
Modification of registry keys for ransom notes and wallpaper
Disabling Windows recovery and repair via bcdedit
Clearing Windows event logs with wevtutil
file_indicators: Presence of <ID>.exe in user startup folder
network_indicators: No explicit C2 or exfiltration in this report, but ransom note email addresses and possible future variants may include network activity
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for mass process/service termination, especially targeting security and backup software. Alert on deletion of shadow copies via WMI/WMIC and modification of boot configuration with bcdedit. Detect registry changes to legalnoticecaption/legalnoticetext and desktop wallpaper. Flag creation of files with unique ransomware extensions and presence of unknown executables in startup folders. Monitor for event log clearing and silent Recycle Bin emptying. Correlate these behaviors for high-confidence ransomware detection.
